identity.description: Extremely randomized tree ensemble: like a random forest but split thresholds are drawn at RANDOM within each candidate feature's range instead of optimized, and by default each tree sees the full sample (no bootstrap). Trades a little bias for a further variance drop and a much cheaper fit — the smoothing sibling of the forest.

emits.note: classification; averaged leaf class fractions — random thresholds make the averaged surface smoother than RF's, still center-compressed
via SHAP (TreeExplainer), not native per-row; global impurity/permutation importances are native

bootstrap.note: library default False — each tree fits the FULL sample; randomness comes from feature subsets + random thresholds, not resampling. Setting true enables oob_score like RF

invariances.why: random thresholds are drawn uniformly over each feature's observed [min,max]; an affine rescale maps that uniform draw equivariantly, leaving the tree distribution unchanged

unlike best-split trees, cut points are drawn uniformly over the feature's RANGE, not its order statistics — a nonlinear monotone transform (log, rank) changes where random cuts land and thus the fitted ensemble in distribution
sklearn >=1.6 extends random missing-value routing to the random splitter; a driver pinned below 1.6 must impute — version-gated, hence empirical
sklearn trees require numeric input; categoricals must be pre-encoded
non-parametric partitions; no assumption on marginal or error distribution
the extra randomization decorrelates trees even without bootstrap, holding up at small n; random splits skip the threshold search so large-n fits are cheaper than RF
piecewise-constant leaves; predictions clamp at the training range boundary

featureStats.why: random thresholds waste splits when few features are informative; low n/p compounds this because each wasted cut costs scarce rows — a gate toward RF/linear
full-sample trees (no bootstrap) all see the same skew; severe imbalance shifts the honest metric to PR-AUC/lift and suggests class_weight='balanced'
uniform random cuts over [min,max] concentrate in empty range when a feature is heavy-tailed — the one tree family where unskewing an input genuinely changes the fit

modelMetrics.why: the direct read on whether the data rewards smoothing (ET wins: random cuts average into a lower-variance surface) or optimized thresholds (RF wins: signal lives at sharp cut points)
one feature owning most importance is the leakage-dominance signature the promotion gate blocks

edgeCases.behavior: even random-split decorrelation cannot average away variance from so few rows; CV is unstable
uniform threshold draws over the stretched range land in empty space, producing near-vacuous splits
random cuts on near-empty dummy columns are almost always uninformative; importance diluted
leakage signature; ensemble degenerates toward one variable's rule

driver.threadSafety: n_jobs-parallel fit and predict; fitted estimator is read-only thread-safe

canBeSeeds.note: a cheap, differently-biased base that diversifies a stack containing RF/GBT

placementClaims.why: learned NaN routing (driver floor sklearn>=1.6) makes upstream imputation unnecessary and it can erase the missingness signal
NOT monotone-invariant: random cuts are uniform over the observed range, so unskewing a heavy-tailed feature places candidate thresholds where the data mass lives
affine rescaling maps the uniform threshold draw equivariantly — the fit is unchanged in distribution
sklearn trees need categoricals encoded to numeric before fit
